findings.claim: RULE-TEMPLATE.md §3.3 annotation contract is not fully closed from R1 COR-TEMPLATE-002. Two residual inaccuracies introduced by the fix-round-1 edit: (a) the text still reads 'SCP-EXXX (where XXX = a new code or a reuse)' implying rule proposals may or must claim their own SCP-E infrastructure code — no such mechanism exists; (b) the fix-round-1 removed the only description of the annotate=true rule-specific annotation (where title=<rule_id>, i.e. SCP-R-NNN is the annotation TITLE) and replaced it with 'Rule ID (in annotation message)' which is accurate only for the first annotation's message text, not for the second annotation's title field. The R1 mitigation's key phrase — 'no separate SCP-E code is reserved per rule' — was not included.
findings.evidence: RULE-TEMPLATE.md §3.3 current text: 'Error code (annotation title=): SCP-EXXX (where XXX = a new code or a reuse — see ADOPT-001 §12.7.7 for the active set). Examples: SCP-E003 for a deny, SCP-E006 for a disabled-rule observability record.' and 'Rule ID (in annotation message): SCP-R-NNN. The rule ID appears in the human-readable message (e.g. SCP-R-002: waivers.json schema violation), separate from the error-code title field.' Actual policy-check.yml 'Render deny annotations' step: first annotation always emits ::error file=...,title=SCP-E003::policy deny triggered by {rule_id}; second annotation (annotate=true path) emits ::error file=...,title={rule_id}::{message} — the RULE ID is the annotation title= in the second emit, not in the message. ADOPT-001 §12.7.7 error-code table lists SCP-E001 through SCP-E007 and SCP-FRESH-001 as a closed infrastructure set; no per-rule SCP-E code column exists. R1 COR-TEMPLATE-002 mitigation explicitly stated: 'rule-specific title=SCP-R-NNN (the rule ID is the annotation title; no separate SCP-E code is reserved per rule)' — this language was not implemented in fix-round-1.
findings.impact: A rule proposal author reading §3.3 after fix-round-1 will: (a) expect to 'claim a new SCP-E code' for their rule because 'a new code or a reuse' remains in the text, creating a false process expectation and potential erroneous D-NNN rows reserving phantom E-codes; (b) be unaware that the annotate=true path emits a second annotation where title=SCP-R-NNN, so they will not document this annotation's title field correctly in their proposal's §3.3 section. Downstream rule-RFC reviews could approve proposals with incorrectly documented annotation contracts, requiring amendment PRs when the rule implementation reveals the true contract.
findings.mitigation: Amend §3.3 to: (1) change 'SCP-EXXX (where XXX = a new code or a reuse)' to 'SCP-E003 for a deny (infrastructure code shared by all rules; rules do NOT claim their own SCP-E codes — the SCP-E code space is a closed infrastructure set at ADOPT-001 §12.7.7)'; (2) add a second bullet: 'Rule-specific annotation (emitted when annotate=true): ::error title=SCP-R-NNN::<message>. The rule ID (SCP-R-NNN) is the annotation title= field in this emit; the message field contains the human-readable finding text. Document the expected message format here.' This brings §3.3 into alignment with the actual two-annotation contract in policy-check.yml and with the R1 mitigation's stated intent.
